summary: Appends a string to a linked list whose control block lives at (*this)+64 (four dwords: head at +0x40, tail at +0x44, aux at +0x48, count at +0x4C). Allocates an 8-byte buffer via OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper, prefills it with 0 at +0 and -1 at +4, fills it with a copy of the input through StringCopyWithBufferRealloc, then allocates a 12-byte node holding the string pointer at +0, 0 at +4 and a byte flag of 1 at +8, and links it either as the new tail (non-empty list) or as head/aux/tail (empty list), incrementing the count.

local_names.this: object whose dereferenced pointer at +0 locates the list control block
local_names.a2: input string to copy and append
local_names.v5: string buffer pointer, or 0 when that allocation failed
local_names.v6: int pointer to the list control block at (*this)+64
local_names.result: allocated list node, or 0 on any allocation failure

operations.description: Allocate an 8-byte string buffer via OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper(8); the allocation result gates the string-copy branch
Initialize the buffer: dword 0 at +0 and -1 at +4, then StringCopyWithBufferRealloc(a2) fills it with a copy of the input string
If the 8-byte allocation failed, the string pointer v5 is 0 and no node is created
v6 = (int*)(*this + 64) locates the list control block one level past the object pointer stored at this+0
Allocate a 12-byte list node via OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper(12); on success the node stores the string pointer at +0, 0 at +4 and 1 as a byte flag at +8
If the 12-byte node allocation failed, result stays 0 and the node is not linked into the list
Non-empty-list path: previous tail's next pointer is set to the new node, tail at obj+0x44 advances, and count at obj+0x4C increments
Empty-list path: head at obj+0x40, aux at obj+0x48 and tail at obj+0x44 all become the new node, and count at obj+0x4C is set to 1
Returns the linked node pointer on success, or 0 when either allocation failed
Reached from ResourceListCleanup (00404d50) and ConfigIniParser (00421cd0) as a shared string-list append helper

clean_pseudocode: if (node) { node[0] = v5; node[1] = 0; node[8] = 1; } else node = 0;
else { v6[0] = node; v6[2] = node; v6[1] = node; v6[3] = 1; }

Semantics of the byte flag at node+8 set to 1 and of the -1 prefill in the string buffer's second dword are unknown.
Owner class of the list control block is unknown; callers span config parsing and resource-list management.
